main_body: Snow-covered log cabin: a large snowy roof slope over a log wall with a plank door and two shuttered, lit windows
top_band: Snow roof, white to pale blue-grey, rows ~8-35 down the middle column, ending in a lighter snow lip with icicles at rows ~33-36
evidence: In a column through the middle, the roof is a tall snow slope (rows 8-35) with a bright snow lip and icicles at the front edge. Directly under it is a dark brown shadow band (rows 37-39) where the eave shades the wall. The log wall (rows 40-62) has an inset door with iron straps and windows set back behind shutters and sills. The roof reads as a visible top surface in the same way as the reference building roofs, so this is a true 3/4 building rather than a front elevation.

style.evidence: The snow has about 5 lightness steps (white, pale blue, light grey-blue, mid blue-grey, shadow blue) in clumps with per-patch variation. The wood is outlined in dark brown and has plank and log grain. The windows have glow gradients, the door has iron straps, and there are icicles and a stone chimney. No large flat fills. Tile density is comparable to the references.
